title: Revealed Social Networks
abstract: arXiv:2501.02609v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The linear-in-means model is the standard empirical model of peer effects and asks that an agent's choice or outcome is a combination of their ideal point and the mean outcome of their group. Using choice data and exogenous group variation, we develop a revealed preference style test for the linear-in-means model. This test is formulated as a linear program and can be interpreted as a condition about differentiating the behavior of each agent in a consistent manner. We then study the identification properties of the linear-in-means model. A key takeaway from our analysis is the close relationship between the dimension of the outcome variable and identification. When the outcome variable is one-dimensional, failures of identification are generic. When the outcome variable is multi-dimensional, we provide natural conditions under which identification is generic.

translated_abstract: arXiv:2501.02609v3 公告类型：替换  摘要：线性均值模型是同伴效应的标准实证模型，假设个体的选择或结果是由其理想点与所在群体平均结果的组合决定的。利用选择数据和外部群体变化，我们为线性均值模型开发了一种揭示性偏好风格的检验方法。该检验被表述为一个线性规划，可被解释为以一致方式区分每个个体行为的一个条件。随后，我们研究了线性均值模型的识别性质。我们分析的一个关键结论是结果变量的维度与识别之间的紧密关系。当结果变量为一维时，识别失败是普遍的。当结果变量为多维时，我们提供了在自然条件下识别普遍成立的充分条件。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于揭示性偏好的线性均值模型检验方法，并发现结果变量维度对模型识别至关重要：一维结果下识别普遍失败，多维结果下在特定条件下识别普遍成功。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a revealed preference test for the linear-in-means model and shows that identification critically depends on outcome dimensionality: generic failure in one dimension, but generic success under natural conditions in multiple dimensions.
